requirement: v3.5.2 fixes the G4 renumber boundary found by the 2026-11-19 dsh-fix real-machine reverification: image/offload events store event references in data.targets[].seq, which the renumber traversal did not rewrite because it only maps *Seq/*Seqs keys. After an edit that shifts indices the installed Harness refused the log with RENUMBER_RUNTIME_REJECTED (a safe, zero-write refusal), so a repaired session could not be renumbered when the edit preceded a target. The fix maps every image/offload data.targets[i].seq through the same old->new mapping, refuses a deleted/out-of-range target with the named RENUMBER_DANGLING_REFERENCE code (zero write, no .bak), keeps the event's own top-level seq assigned only from its dense position, and leaves other lowercase seq fields untouched. No other behaviour changes.

assertions.boundary_source: docs/acceptance/3.5.1/RELEASE-3510-DSH-FIX-REAL-MACHINE.json records the real-machine finding: --delete-seq 0 on the repaired log is refused by the installed Harness with RENUMBER_RUNTIME_REJECTED ("invalid seed event at index 2795: image/offload: image index 0 does not exist", zero write) while --delete-seq 2795 (post-target) passes runtime_verified true
assertions.fix_scope: src/backup/renumber.mjs runs rewriteImageOffloadTargets() after the *Seq/*Seqs walk, scoped to events whose top-level type is image/offload; each integer data.targets[i].seq is mapped old->new; the event top-level seq is still assigned from its dense position; inserted image/offload events are mapped against pre-edit seqs
assertions.refusal: a deleted or out-of-range target returns the reused named code RENUMBER_DANGLING_REFERENCE with detail.references[0] = {event_type:"image/offload", key:"seq", at:"data.targets[0].seq", seq, deleted}, writes nothing and leaves no .bak
assertions.tests: test/fix-renumber.test.mjs 38/38 (+8): single target rewritten with exact data JSON and mapping, multiple targets all rewritten, deleting the target event itself -> named refusal + zero write + no .bak, deleting an event after the target -> target unchanged, own seq vs target seq not confused, non-image/offload lowercase seq not rewritten, out-of-range target -> same refusal; one runtime-gated case proves the fixture is runtime-valid, shows the unrewritten variant refused by the installed Harness, then asserts plan.validation.runtime_verified true / future_append_evidence installed-harness and that the applied log passes
assertions.regression: test/backup-verify.test.mjs 25/25; combined affected suites green; eslint 0 errors; layer-check clean; mojibake clean
assertions.docs: docs/BACKUP-DESIGN.md §20.1 reference rule and §20.2 pipeline now state the image/offload data.targets[].seq rule and the RENUMBER_DANGLING_REFERENCE refusal; §20.5 coverage list updated; CHANGELOG has the 3.5.2 entry
